findings.label: Cutaneous gumma
findings.evidence: Caption: 'disfiguring gummatous lesions infiltrating the skin of the nose, glabella, and forehead, with clustered nodules in the left interciliary region'; image shows nodular and crusted facial lesions.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a boy with gummatous facial lesions consistent with endemic syphilis (bejel), explicitly supported by the caption and article title.
panels.attribution_text: Abdolrasouli et al. A case of endemic syphilis, Iran.. Emerging infectious diseases 2013. doi:10.3201/eid1901.120756. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure Figure.
panels.figure_caption: Disfiguring infiltration of the nose, glabella, and forehead with clustered nodules in left interciliary region of boy with endemic syphilis, Iran, 2010.
in_text_mentions: Examination revealed disfiguring gummatous lesions infiltrating the skin of the nose, glabella, and forehead, with clustered nodules in the left interciliary region (Figure). No other abnormality was found. He denied any sexual contacts, and there were no stigmata of congenital syphilis. Skin biopsy was refused. Tuberculin skin test results were negative. Full blood count, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and C-reactive protein level were within reference ranges.
